cves.summary: Insufficiently protected credentials in GitHub Copilot and Visual Studio Code allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network.
cves.headline: GitHub Copilot and VS Code before 1.136.2 leak credentials over the network

cves.summary: Stable Diffusion WebUI through 1.10.1 contains a credential disclosure vulnerability in the /sdapi/v1/cmd-flags endpoint that returns parsed command-line arguments including gradio_auth and api_auth values in cleartext.
cves.headline: Stable Diffusion WebUI through 1.10.1 leaks API credentials from cmd-flags endpoint

name: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
title: CWE-522: Insufficiently Protected Credentials
ai_text: In AI software this weakness shows up in developer facing tools and model interfaces that handle API keys and login secrets. The two CVEs here sit in a coding assistant, GitHub Copilot and VS Code, and in a model interface, Gradio's Stable Diffusion WebUI. Both reach the flaw through ordinary network or endpoint access rather than any deep break in the model itself. Copilot and VS Code before 1.136.2 leak credentials over the network, and Stable Diffusion WebUI through 1.10.1 exposes API credentials from its cmd-flags endpoint. An attacker who can observe or query those paths can retrieve credentials, then use them to reach the accounts and services those keys unlock.
description: The product transmits or stores authentication credentials, but it uses an insecure method that is susceptible to unauthorized interception and/or retrieval.

mitigations.description: Use an appropriate security mechanism to protect the credentials.
Make appropriate use of cryptography to protect the credentials.
Use industry standards to protect the credentials (e.g. LDAP, keystore, etc.).

consequences.note: An attacker could gain access to user accounts and access sensitive data used by the user accounts.
